newsitem.title: USA: Congress nixes plan to extend check clearing schedule.
newsitem.headline: Congress nixes plan to extend check clearing schedule.

text.p: Leading members of Congress said Friday they would oppose a legislative proposal from the Federal Reserve to let banks hold local checks for an additional day.
Consumer groups were up in arms over the plan to let banks hold consumer deposits for three days instead of two as allowed under current law.
There is "little prospect for Congressional action," House Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach, said.

"The additional day will have minimal impact on forgeries, the largest portion of check fraud," Leach said. "By holding to the two-day limit, Congress encourages the advancement of check clearing technology while giving working families earlier access to their much needed resources."
The ranking Democrat on the panel, Representative Henry Gonzalez of Texas, first urged Leach to oppose the plan in a letter two weeks ago.
Banks would have collected millions of dollars in additional interest by holding the funds for an additional day, consumer groups have said.
